prompt:
Write 12 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck and back strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1358; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: First notice of loss received for a low-speed collision in a parking lot involving the insured's vehicle and a second vehicle. The claimant reports neck and back strain and is not represented by counsel.

Entry 2: Confirmed the driver is named on the policy and that coverage was in force at the time of the loss. No issues with the policy status were found.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact and notes the scene as described.

Entry 4: Spoke with the other driver, who gave an account of the collision that matches what the claimant reported. Witness statements were requested and are being collected.

Entry 5: Reviewed the photographs submitted by the claimant and the scene images. The vehicle damage is consistent with the impact described and the reported injury fits the force of the crash.

Entry 6: Ran a prior claims and vehicle history search. No earlier damage to the vehicle is on record, and nothing suggests the damage predates the policy start.

Entry 7: Called the claimant to take a recorded statement. The account given is the same as the one provided at first notice.

Entry 8: Requested medical records from the treating provider. The claimant reports ongoing neck and back pain and has been attending regular physical therapy sessions.

Entry 9: Medical records show a small strain in the same area several years ago that healed fully, with no treatment since. The claimant was asked about it and acknowledged the earlier episode.

Entry 10: Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for a strain of this kind. Requested a treatment plan and expected timeline from the provider to better understand the duration.

Entry 11: Reviewed the treatment plan with the medical reviewer, who noted the injury pattern is consistent with the collision. Duration is being monitored against standard recovery guidelines.

Entry 12: Claimant has been contacted for an update on current symptoms and work status. File remains open pending receipt of the updated treatment plan and witness statements.
